questions.stem: A projectile must reach 80 m on level ground; what minimum launch speed in m/s is needed?
questions.explanation: v_min = sqrt(Rg) = sqrt(80*9.8) = sqrt(784) = 28.0 m/s. The 45-degree angle gives this minimum.
questions.hint: Square root of range times gravity.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Direction of the centripetal acceleration
questions.learningObjective: Explain why centripetal acceleration is inward
questions.stem: Explain why centripetal acceleration must point toward the center of the circle.

answer.exemplar: The velocity vector is always tangent to the circle, so to keep the object on the circular path the acceleration must pull it inward, perpendicular to velocity, changing direction without changing speed.

questions.explanation: Inward acceleration continuously redirects the tangential velocity. Without it the object would travel in a straight line.
questions.hint: Inward pull changes direction, not speed.

questions.stem: Explain why 30 and 60 degrees give the same range for the same launch speed.

answer.exemplar: Because range depends on sin(2 theta), and sin(60) equals sin(120), so 30 and 60 degrees (doubling to 60 and 120) yield identical sine values and identical ranges.

questions.explanation: Range uses sin(2θ); complementary angles produce the same sine value, hence equal ranges. The maximum remains at 45 degrees.
questions.hint: Range depends on sin of two theta.
